text.cover.title:
Powerded
by Superheros
text.s1.cap1:
The spaces available for the evening
are generous. Their layout, however,
remains highly fragmented.
text.s2.cap1:
They divide into five main zones,
each one cut off from the others.
text.s3.cap1:
On top of this fragmentation,
the two ballrooms, Zurich and Geneva,
stand far apart
from each other.
text.s4.cap1:
The key issue therefore becomes the flow
between these two rooms: it must stay
as smooth as possible. To achieve this,
we adopt a served / servant logic.
text.s4.p1:
On the right, the main circulation
of the guests.
text.s4.p2:
On the left, the service circulation:
cloakroom, toilets, technical access.
text.h1.cap1:
In the 1950s and 1960s,
superheroes rose to become
icons of American
popular culture.
text.h2.cap1:
The comic book became their
natural territory. There it invented
a visual language designed to be
direct, popular and spectacular.
text.h3.cap1:
Printed fast and cheap,
these comics turned the dot
screen into a visual signature,
iconic almost by accident.
text.h4.cap1:
In the 1960s, Roy Lichtenstein
isolated and enlarged these codes.
The dot screen, or Ben Day dots,
became his signature and brought
the comic book into Pop Art.
text.h5.cap1:
Explosions, impacts, flashes
and onomatopoeia then became
graphic signs that read at once.
This is the vocabulary
we make our own for the evening.
text.dens.cap1:
Pop Art works through accumulation, saturation and impact.
To be convincing, its world must be generous, dense, immersive.
text.dens.cap2:
The context sets a particularly tight equation:
a huge space to dress, 800 to 850 guests, a low ceiling,
many functional elements to fit in (stage, bars, buffets,
high tables, lounges), and a decoration budget capped at €40k.
text.dens.cap3:
Trying to decorate the whole space would dilute this budget,
and the visual impact along with it.
text.big.cap1:
The elements the event cannot do without
become the scenography itself.
text.big.cap2:
Seen in plan, the room reads like a monumental Pop Art painting
after Lichtenstein: the explosion becomes the stage, the sparks
spread out into lines of bars and buffets, the dot screen
takes shape as rows of high tables and furniture.
text.big.cap3:
As the room fills up, the guests complete the composition
and bring it to life. They are in the picture, they compose it.
text.axo.cap1:
The composition also organises the flows. The stage anchors
the far end of the main room, the grid of high tables guides
the guests through the space, bars and lounges settle
around the edges, the cloakroom and services stay
in the background, following the served / servant logic.
text.sc-txt.cap1:
An explosive scenography to carry
the high point of the evening: the 90-minute
live concert played by the teams.
text.sc-txt.cap2:
The same stage then welcomes the DJ
to tip the evening into party mode.
text.sc-txt.cap3:
A Pop Art explosion bursts from the floor
and the walls, and makes the stage
the focal point of the whole room.
text.pc-txt.cap1:
Relive the golden age of superheroes from the inside,
at the foot of the Daily Planet, renamed
for the occasion: “Our Daily Planet”.
text.pc-txt.cap2:
An immersive photocall where every guest
steps into the comic panel,
right in the heart of the explosion.
